also: put it back in the toolbox

evidence: Col. 1.6: et intrā id ipsum clausus locus, quō ferrāmenta condantur
terms.comment: A description of ours: arca, a chest, with ferrāmenta, the iron tools. We have found no ancient or modern word for a toolbox in Lewis & Short, Traupman, Morgan–Owens, or Levi–Bini. Columella has the farm’s iron tools kept in a closed place of their own inside the store-room.

terms.gloss: a small box for tools, one you carry
terms.comment: Also ours: cistula, a little box or basket (Plautus), for a small toolbox with a handle.

phrases.english: Put the hammer back in the toolbox.

phrases.latin: sitque utrīque proximum horreum, quō cōnferātur omne rūsticum īnstrūmentum; et intrā id ipsum clausus locus, quō ferrāmenta condantur
phrases.english: and next to both let there be a store-room, into which all the farm equipment is gathered; and inside it a closed place where the iron tools are put away

sources: Lewis & Short: ferramentum · Lewis & Short: arca · Lewis & Short: cistula
